title: spring itinerary for the unknown
content:
from my podcast: botanical studies of internet magic
listen on spotify / listen on apple

today is an atmospheric map for our slow transition from winter into spring — through the archetypes of Pisces, Aries, and Taurus. we'll explore how to work with these energies in deepening into the creative life.

I'll share why thinking in seasons has become such an important practice for me, and my intentions for this coming season, along with personal life context. we'll dive into the three archetypes and their grounding theme words: Pisces (dreaming), Aries (instinct), Taurus (embodying), as well as the questions they invite us to contemplate.

this itinerary is the 12 week map for season 2 of Labyrinth Library, which opens Monday.

autumn itinerary for the unknown

In today's episode, I want to share my atmospheric navigational map for these next 12 weeks as we transition from winter to spring. And I think of it as an open-ended itinerary, not of fixed destinations, but a general felt sense or texture of these next three months, inspired by the astrological archetypes of Pisces, Aries, and Taurus.

Last year, I shared an episode, Autumn Itinerary for the Unknown, in which I talked about Libra, Scorpio, and Sagittarius as guides for us to move from fall into winter, this gentle dissension into the darkness, through the themes of holding complexity, being underground in the underworld, and coming back up again to quest and to expand.

And so in this season, I've centered on three key words, anchoring themes for each astrological sign. For Pisces, the word is dreaming. For Aries, the word is instinct. And for Taurus, the word is embodying. I want to explore and unpack these three archetypes with you in this episode, and see how each archetype can be a grounding anchor for living into this season in relation to our creative practices and projects, and invite us to look at it from different perspectives through the energy of each archetype.

Before we explore that together, first, let's talk about why think about time in the span of seasons or 12 weeks unfolding over a season. And I also want to share my personal intentions for this coming season, a personal life update, as well as tell you about my seasonal community, Labyrinth, that will be a community container for exploring this itinerary together.

why think in seasons

It took me a while to come to terms with what it feels like to think and live seasonally because our society is so linear. We've been conditioned to think that life is just one steady march up a large mountain, and you should always be working eight hours a day, and that you should aim for one conquest after another, when in reality, seasonal time is to be with cyclical time, to feel into the texture of how time can be experienced in its ebb and flow as something elastic, and to notice the micro increments of a season is to celebrate the small shifts, rather than letting time blur past as one long road.

Two experiences that have really helped me be sensitive to this is in leading Labyrinth last autumn and collaborating with a friend, LJ, on atmospheres, a writing practice marked by the astrological decans.

For me right now, in my mid-30s, time feels like it's both in this total stasis, and it feels like it's accelerating. Maybe it's age, maybe it's being at a precipice of different lives and uncertainty. Maybe it's oscillating between the terror of sometimes feeling like nothing is happening, like this will be my life forever, and then sometimes experiencing time as this one long blur, like where has all the time gone? Where have the years gone?

And so I find that working with seasons as a container for holding time, looking at a season as if it were this giant bowl, and we can feel into the edges of that bowl, we can use it for noticing, for marking, for paying attention to the tiny changes of our lives, it helps me slow down and not feel like I always need to be rushing towards some inevitable destination, but instead to attune to what is here. It's a practice of being more present with where I am, with how I feel, and holding space for change.

When I give my experience of time a vessel-like structure of a season, it helps me feel more safe and it helps focus my energy. This is where I am this season, and by next season it could be something totally different. And of course, there's never a clear boundary. As the seasons change, the borders blur into each other, but creating soft containers in my mind allows me to give my current life experiences, challenges, processes, a sort of bracket, a parentheses, and I can pay attention to them with more patience and tenderness.

my intentions for this season

So to give you a bit of context, let me share where I am in this season and my intentions for this spring. When I think about the key phrases that come up to ground me in my intentions these next couple of months, the words that come to mind are active dreaming, monk life, and daily pleasures.

This actually maps perfectly onto the themes of Pisces, Aries, and Taurus, which we'll explore in just a bit. But all this is to say I'm feeling especially drawn to practicing spiritual discipline, balanced with mundane sensory pleasures, embodiment, eating, walking in nature, and time set aside to fall into the rabbit holes of my creative practice.

For this season, I am living in suburban North Carolina at my parents' house. I've been here since Christmas Day. And I'm here because I recently experienced a pretty major life rupture. Before this, I lived for four years in Istanbul with my partner, my dog, and a home. And that had followed two years of nomadic living. I felt like in those four years, I had slowly, finally settled my restless spirit and found the elements of a life that made me happy and grounded and safe.

And this has never been an easy thing for me. But last year, on top of many other things, my residency permit got rejected and I had to leave my life abruptly behind. With this passage, my sense of the future went from something that felt like a clear, steady path forwards into the static, stormy chaos.

I've been thrown again into this place of displacement and different varieties of loss. And originally, I was planning to travel to resume the semi-nomadic life that I inhabited before settling, but I decided that what I really need now is stillness, silence, inner work, and embodiment.

So I asked myself, what can I do in relative isolation, in suburbia, in North Carolina, that I can't do anywhere else? And the answer came to me as using this time to connect to my unconscious, to my dream worlds, to practicing devotion and discipline, spiritual discipline and daily embodiment, allowing pleasure and letting that do deep work in my system.

As an extremely emotional being, it's been a challenging time for me, but it's often during these times, these seasons of my life that I discover the most precious jewels of wisdom and insights. So bracketing it as a season has really helped me think about how to navigate the unknown.



a labyrinth for walking

And navigating the unknown is the theme of my seasonal community, Labyrinth Library. The spring itinerary I'm about to share with you through Pisces, Aries, and Taurus is the non-linear, non-curriculum of my community. I say non-curriculum because each week I will be sharing one audio artifact teaching relating to the astrological archetype of this season, but the purpose of Labyrinth as a 12-week community container is to help you navigate your own labyrinths.

The labyrinth is one of my favorite metaphors. It's a spiraling garden path that you can't really get lost in. It's not a maze, but you are guided to be present in process, in the wandering, to move towards your own center. So we are all each in our own labyrinths. No one can walk your path for you, but we can be together in the process of navigating what we don't know, of looking at the unknown together.

And so my intention with Labyrinth is to offer that creative companionship, to be a witness and to be seen in the process, to ask the hard questions with no clear answers and explore them together. The purpose of this community container is about companionship and guidance through your practices and processes. And for me, it is a vessel into which I can share my real-time creative work, digestions, experiments, systems, and inspirations.

Season two starts on Monday, and I'd be very happy for you to join me. So let's talk about the itinerary for these next three months.

pisces → dreaming

On February 19th through March 20th, I'll transition into Pisces season. Pisces is mutable water ruled by Jupiter and Neptune. My anchoring word, key theme for Pisces, is the word dreaming.

So I think of Pisces as an invitation to dissolve, to let reality feel fluid, to let yourself be porous, to go on voyages with the imagination and give yourself permission to dwell in the liminal spaces.

I don't know if you've seen the movie Amélie, the French film, it's one of my favorite movies from my teenage years. And there's that scene in Amélie where she, the main character, dissolves and collapses into a puddle of water. That, to me, captures Pisces energy, and it's the willingness to become a puddle in a society that is always forcing us to be solid.

So in Pisces season, I'm excited to experiment with how I can let myself be carried away in a gentle light way, because I am fixed water, I'm a Scorpio, and sometimes the fixed water energy feels so heavy, but Pisces energy feels like living in the shimmering sparkles at the top of the water, being the fish that can jump both out of the water into the sunlight and back deep again. It's letting emotions, dreams, ideas, possibilities wash over you.

And so the questions I want to sit with during Pisces season is how can we resource our sensitivity, our intuition, our poetic sensibility, imagination, emotions? How can we see our qualities as cherished resources? Not to diminish or be embarrassed about, but to elevate and cultivate?

How can we give ourselves sanctioned windows of dreaming time? To enter dream worlds and fantasy landscapes, to do shadow work, but very lightly, very gently, to get lost in the liminal and to bring the wisdom back into the waking real world?

How can we indulge in the parts of ourselves that wants to dissolve, that wants to cry, that wants to be messy and formless and nonlinear? How can we create safe ritual containers for that to surrender ourselves into the whirlpools?

And how can we make fantasy feel more safe? Because indulging in the practice of dreaming, this is not a capitalist culture sanctioned approved way of being, and yet maybe this is exactly what we need. Maybe if you have that impulse to dream inside of you, the work is not about repressing it or feeling guilty about it, but to hold it as sacred to create a ritual for entering and leaving that space.

In Pisces season, we'll be working with honing intuition and sensitivity, journaling, shadow work, active dreaming, meditation, exploring raw creative expressions, emotional voyaging, and thinking about psychic practices.

Pisces is also about boundaries, the boundary between what is real and what is imagined, what is me and what is you, the boundaries between places, between digital, physical, emotional worlds, and how can the liminality, the transition between these spaces be in itself a safe, fertile place to dwell in and not to fear?

I don't know about you, but I am very excited for Pisces season.

aries → instinct

Then on March 21st through April 19th, we will enter Aries. Aries as cardinal fire ruled by Mars. My anchoring word for Aries season is instinct because Aries is a warrior spirit. It is the first spark. It is the raw impulse that wants to begin a fire, a project, to take action, to do something before the thinking mind can intervene, before the self-doubt can create static or get in the way.

Aries represents that first initial impulse, the animalistic instinct, the hunger. It's the fire that wants to light the match. It's a craving to feel alive. And with it may be a need for adrenaline, intensity, wanting to initiate things, feeling impulsive, pulling the trigger before we fully aimed.

Maybe we'll find that taking aim is not that important. Maybe we'll find that our body knows how to take aim without our minds needing to interfere.

I have an Aries moon, which can feel pretty explosive and intense. With it comes this thirst for novelty, feeling very easily bored, having a very short attention span and a desire to feel excited to feel on fire. I think Aries, well Aries and Scorpio keeps me honest and unable to tolerate bullshit.

The questions we'll ask during Aries season is, how can we practice trusting in our raw instinct and creative impulse? How can we give our creative fire a proper channel so that it doesn't suffocate us or burn us alive? How do we need to get out of our own way?

And just like in Pisces with the practice of dreaming, how can we create a practice for Aries such that it feels safe to trust that instinct to be with your fire energy? Can we create containers, make games for it to play so that it doesn't get bored of itself?

Again, self-trust is the core practice here. It's building a relationship and a sensitivity to your own raw impulses. I think about Ace of Wands energy, tuning into the micro sensations of your tiny desires, letting that spark new projects, new fires, new possibilities.

So the work of trusting your instincts during Aries season is about paying attention to tiny jolts of electricity and sparks within you, your creative body.

taurus → embodying

Starting April 20th until May 20th, we will be in the sign of Taurus, which is fixed earth ruled by Venus. And the anchoring word that I've chosen for Taurus is embodying.

It's after the dreamy waters of Pisces and the fiery instincts of Aries, Taurus season is an invitation to land in the material embodied realm. It's making a home in your body, in yourself, and asking the question of where does home actually live? Where does belonging take place?

And home as trusting yourself, home as trusting your relationship to the lived sensory world, to your daily practices, to your embodiment, to the worlds you create on the internet perhaps.

Sometimes the energy of Pisces can feel a bit disembodied and I find the energy of Taurus very soothing and calming and grounding. It feels like solid earth, Taurus energy feels like laying down on a soft blanket in a lush green place with abundant foods and fruits and birds and bees and perfect spring weather.

It's luxuriating in the daily simple pleasures and using the body as compass, asking ourselves what does our body want? What signals are coming from the body? How can we listen to it instead of allowing it to be overridden by our minds?

Taurus season reminds me to embrace slowness, the rhythm of longer days, of learning how to tend to gardens and practice patience with a sensual pleasure.

Taurus season is an invitation to be with the textures of daily life, making bread, caring for a garden, going on walks, being in the body, being in our relationships with an emphasis on beauty and pleasure and comfort and stability and rootedness.

Taurus feels like a kind of arrival, a sort of homecoming, allowing yourself to feel supported, to trust, to rest.

In Taurus season, I want to ask the question of how can we let the body guide us deeper into our creative practice? How can we create a sense of home in the work, in ourselves, and to trust that foundation as something which will support us and hold us? Like the feeling of leaning back into the earth, laying down and knowing that the earth will hold you, that there is bounty here to nourish you.

Ultimately, Taurus season is about becoming aware of the inherent abundance you hold in the mundane, in your creative body, in the day-to-day experience of life, of yourself, of time, of the seasons.

the invitation

Thinking about this next season, these next 12 weeks, I see this full arc of dreaming in Pisces season, trusting raw instinct and action in Aries season, and grounding in home, in the body, in oneself, embodying your creative practice, your work in the world, your sense of belonging to yourself.

What would it feel like to give these next 12 weeks your full attention, not to optimize it for maximum productivity or to meet some goals? Sometimes I like goals, but I also find that goals can distract us from presence and process, which are pathways to meeting the goals in the first place.

How can we use this time to actually inhabit each week with our fullest attention, to sense into the textures of each week, to listen to what each season, each month, each day, each moment has to reveal?

By the end of these 12 weeks and this next season of Labyrinth, I will be most likely making my way back to Istanbul. I'm very curious what my emotional arc will be like in these next few months of deliberate practice and paying attention.

If you'd like to join me, walk alongside me this coming season, and if you'd like the support and witnessing of a magical group of creative beings, as well as my guidance, resources, and ongoing inspirations, I would love for you to join me in season two of Labyrinth Library in walking our own labyrinths alone and together.

On March 9th, which I heard is a planting day, I will also be starting my business class, Digital Abundance, which sounds perfect for its culmination into Taurus season.

Thank you so much for listening to this episode. If you'd like to explore more of my work, you can visit my website world. The best way to keep in touch with me is my newsletter. You can explore more of my other courses or working together one-on-one. Until next time, take care.
